person: Lan Tran is a 41-year-old pharmacy technician who works rotating shifts and reads official English slowly. She holds power of attorney for her mother, Hoa Tran, 77, who lives with her family. Lan handles her mother's retirement accounts and tax papers on her phone, and her comfort with technology is low. The preparer's draft return shows a penalty for a distribution missed from the IRA her mother inherited from her brother. Lan does not understand why, and she worries it will cost money. She wants every step explained in simple words and wants to be asked before any money moves.
stated_up_front: Hello, I help my mother with her retirement money. The tax man sent a paper saying a penalty of $1,500, I do not understand. Can you check and fix it? Please ask me before you pay or take any money.

facts.truth: 3 March 1949, so she is 77 now and turned 76 in 2025.
Mr. Tran, born 1953, four years younger, alive and living in the same house.

facts.about: Pinebrook traditional IRA value on 31 December 2025

facts.truth: About $38,500. Her mother has never taken money from it and wants to leave it alone.
The plan already paid her mother $4,800 in July 2026 by itself. Lan wants no more taken from it.

facts.about: Harborline IRA in her mother's own name
facts.truth: About $61,000. Her mother took $2,700 out in June, and a $2,000 withdrawal is scheduled for December.
It came from her mother's brother, Uncle Bay, who died in 2024. It was worth about $86,000 on 31 December 2024.

facts.about: The 2025 distribution missed from the inherited IRA
facts.truth: About $6,000 was not taken. The preparer's draft shows a $1,500 penalty, which is 25% of that.
A letter from the IRS says 2024 was forgiven. The preparer still drafted a form for 2024.
An adviser emailed saying to take the missed money from her mother's own IRA. A fee service also emailed offering to get the penalty removed for 20% of what it saves.
Her mother wants each IRA to pay its own distribution and does not want any extra money taken out.
Lan will not pay anyone a fee. She paid an application helper before and got nothing useful.
